questions.question: A dealer mixes 26 kg of a variety of tea at ₹200 per kg with 30 kg of another variety of tea at ₹360 per kg, and sells the mixture at ₹300 per kg. His profit percentage is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A dealer mixes 26 kg of tea at ₹200 per kg with 30 kg of tea at ₹360 per kg, and sells the mixture at ₹300 per kg.

**Formula used:**

Cost Price (CP) = dfrac{{Total Cost of Tea}}{{Total Weight}}

Profit Percentage = dfrac{{Selling Price (SP) - Cost Price (CP)}}{{Cost Price (CP)}} times 100

**Calculation:**

Cost of 26 kg tea = 26 × ₹200 = ₹5200

Cost of 30 kg tea = 30 × ₹360 = ₹10800

Total weight = 26 + 30 = 56 kg

Total cost = ₹5200 + ₹10800 = ₹16000

⇒ Cost Price (CP) per kg = dfrac{₹16000}{56}

⇒ CP = ₹285.71 per kg

Selling Price (SP) per kg = ₹300

⇒ Profit Percentage = dfrac{₹300 - ₹285.71}{₹285.71} times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = dfrac{₹14.29}{₹285.71} times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage ≈ 5%

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: If two trains 200 m and 150 m long are running on parallel rails at the rate of 50 km/h and 30 km/h, respectively, find the relative speed if they are running in the same direction.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of Train 1 = 200 m

Length of Train 2 = 150 m

Speed of Train 1 = 50 km/h

Speed of Train 2 = 30 km/h

Direction: Same

**Formula used:**

Relative Speed = |Speed₁ - Speed₂|

1 km/h = dfrac{5}{18} m/s

**Calculation:**

Speed of Train 1 = 50 × dfrac{5}{18} = dfrac{250}{18} m/s

Speed of Train 2 = 30 × dfrac{5}{18} = dfrac{150}{18} m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = dfrac{250}{18} - dfrac{150}{18}

⇒ Relative Speed = dfrac{100}{18} m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = dfrac{50}{9} m/s

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

• The structure is an excellent example of **Mughal architecture** with no use of iron or wood in its construction.

• The Bara Imambara is a unique blend of **Persian and Mughal architectural styles**.
 
• The entire structure was built without any supporting beams or iron, showcasing advanced engineering techniques of the era.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula commissioned the project during a famine to provide **daily wages to laborers**, reflecting his commitment to public welfare.
 
• The construction employed thousands of workers, both skilled and unskilled, as a famine relief measure.
 
 
 
• **Bhool Bhulaiya:**
 
 
• The labyrinth is a network of interconnected passages designed to confuse intruders and also served as a strategic defense mechanism.
 
• It is a major tourist attraction and adds a mysterious charm to the structure.

• The Bara Imambara is an important religious site for **Shia Muslims**, as it serves as a congregation hall for religious ceremonies, particularly during the month of Muharram.

• It is a major festival in **Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh,** and parts of Nepal, observed to honor the **Sun God (Surya Dev)** and his consort **Chhathi Maiya**.
 
• The festival spans **four days** and includes rituals like fasting, holy bathing in rivers, and offering Arghya (water offering) to the setting and rising sun.
 
• Chhath Puja is known for its emphasis on **purity, devotion, and environmental harmony**.
 
• The main rituals are conducted along riverbanks, with devotees preparing offerings such as **thekua, fruits, and sugarcane**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Chhathi Maiya**:
 
 
• Chhathi Maiya is worshipped as the **goddess of fertility and health**.

• Day 2: **Kharna** – A day-long fast is broken with a simple meal, followed by a 36-hour nirjala (waterless) fast.
 
• Day 3: **Sandhya Arghya** – Offerings are made to the setting sun at riverbanks.
 
• Day 4: **Usha Arghya** – Rituals conclude with offerings to the rising sun.

• The festival traces its roots to ancient Vedic rituals, where the Sun God was revered as a sustainer of life.
 
• It is mentioned in texts like the Rigveda, highlighting the importance of solar worship.

questions.question: What is the salt measurement in hypersaline lagoons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**More than 100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hypersaline lagoons** are characterized by extremely high salinity levels, often exceeding **100 ppt (parts per thousand)**.
 
• These salinity levels occur due to **intense evaporation rates** and limited water exchange with open seas or freshwater sources.
 
• Such lagoons are typically found in **arid or semi-arid regions** where evaporation surpasses precipitation.
 
• Examples of hypersaline lagoons include **Laguna Madre (Texas, USA)** and various lagoons in the Middle East and Australia.
 
• The high salinity environment supports **specialized organisms** such as halophilic bacteria and algae, adapted to thrive in extreme conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salinity Measurement:**

 
 
• Salinity is usually measured in **parts per thousand (ppt)**, representing the amount of dissolved salts in water.
 
• Normal seawater salinity is approximately **35 ppt**, whereas hypersaline environments exceed **100 ppt**.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation and Salinity:**
 
 
• **Evaporation** is a key factor in hypersaline lagoons, significantly increasing salinity by removing water and concentrating salts.
 
• The absence of significant freshwater input further exacerbates salinity levels.
 
 
 
• **Halophiles:**
 
 
• Organisms such as **halophilic bacteria and archaea** are specially adapted to survive in high-salinity environments.
 
• These organisms play essential roles in nutrient cycles within hypersaline ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Importance:**
 
 
• Hypersaline lagoons are unique ecosystems, providing habitats for specialized species.
 
• They act as natural laboratories for studying **extremophile organisms** and their adaptations.

questions.question: Name the Sri Lankan Buddhist text that provides details of the Mauryan empire.

__
 
• **Dipavamsa** is an ancient Buddhist chronicle written in the **Pali language** in Sri Lanka.
 
• It is considered the **earliest extant historical record** of Sri Lanka, dating back to the 3rd-4th century CE.
 
• The text provides valuable insights into the **history of the Mauryan Empire**, particularly Emperor Ashoka's role in spreading Buddhism.
 
• It documents the arrival of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, including the **mission of Mahinda**, Emperor Ashoka's son, who introduced Buddhism to the island.
 
• Dipavamsa served as a precursor to the later and more detailed Sri Lankan chronicle, the **Mahavamsa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahavamsa:**

 
 
• The **Mahavamsa** is another significant Buddhist chronicle of Sri Lanka written in Pali, continuing the historical record found in the Dipavamsa.
 
• It provides a more detailed and structured account of Sri Lankan history and Buddhism compared to the Dipavamsa.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Texts:**
 
 
• The **Ashokavadana** is a Buddhist text that narrates the life and deeds of Emperor Ashoka but is not specific to Sri Lankan history.
 
• The **Divyavadana** is a collection of Buddhist legends, also focusing on Ashoka and his contributions to Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Emperor Ashoka:**
 
 
• Ashoka was a Mauryan emperor who played a pivotal role in the spread of Buddhism in India and beyond.
 
• His son, Mahinda, and daughter, Sanghamitta, are credited with propagating Buddhism in Sri Lanka.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Dipavamsa:**
 
 
• Dipavamsa serves as an essential source for understanding the cultural and religious history of ancient Sri Lanka.
 
• It highlights the impact of Indian influence, particularly through the Mauryan Empire, on Sri Lankan society and religion.

questions.question: Which of the following is the quality of the public goods?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-rivalrous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Public goods** are characterized as **non-rivalrous**, meaning that the consumption of the good by one person does not reduce its availability for others (e.g., national defense, street lighting).
 
• Non-rivalry ensures that no matter how many people use the good, its supply remains unaffected for others.
 
• Examples of non-rivalrous goods include public parks, clean air, and national security.
 
• Public goods are often provided by governments because private markets may fail to offer them due to their non-rivalrous and non-excludable nature.
 
• Non-rivalry is a key component in distinguishing public goods from private goods, which are rivalrous in consumption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Excludable vs Non-excludable:**

 
 
• **Excludable goods** are those where it is possible to prevent someone from using them (e.g., private goods like a meal in a restaurant).
 
• **Non-excludable goods**, such as public goods, are accessible to everyone (e.g., national defense).
 
 
 
• **Rivalrous vs Non-rivalrous:**
 
 
• **Rivalrous goods** are those that can only be consumed by one person at a time (e.g., a sandwich).
 
• **Non-rivalrous goods** can be consumed by many people simultaneously without depletion (e.g., a lighthouse's signal).
 
 
 
• **Free Rider Problem:**
 
 
• The free rider problem arises with public goods because people can benefit from them without contributing to their cost.
 
• This often leads to under-provision of such goods in a free market, necessitating government intervention.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Public Goods:**
 
 
• Examples include clean air, national defense, public broadcasting, and street lighting.
 
• These goods are typically funded through taxation to ensure universal access.

questions.question: According to the Indian calendar, the March and April months are known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaitra-Vaisakha**__.

__
 
• In the Indian calendar, the months of March and April correspond to **Chaitra and Vaisakha**.
 
• The Indian calendar, also known as the **Hindu lunar calendar**, is widely used for determining religious festivals and auspicious days.
 
• Chaitra is the **first month** of the Hindu lunar calendar, marking the beginning of the new year in several Indian traditions.
 
• Vaisakha follows Chaitra and is considered the **second month** in the traditional calendar.
 
• Important festivals such as **Ugadi** (Telugu and Kannada New Year) and **Gudi Padwa** (Marathi New Year) are celebrated during the Chaitra month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindu Lunar Calendar:**

 
 
• The Hindu calendar is a **lunisolar calendar**, meaning it accounts for both the phases of the moon and the position of the sun.
 
• It consists of **12 months**, each divided into two fortnights: Shukla Paksha (waxing phase) and Krishna Paksha (waning phase).
 
 
 
• **Chaitra Month:**
 
 
• Chaitra marks the beginning of the spring season and is associated with new beginnings in Indian culture.
 
• It is considered an auspicious time for starting new ventures or religious observances.
 
 
 
• **Vaisakha Month:**
 
 
• Vaisakha is associated with the harvest season and is celebrated in various parts of India with festivals like **Baisakhi** in Punjab.
 
• It also marks the birth anniversary of **Lord Buddha**, celebrated as Buddha Purnima.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations:**
 
 
• The Indian calendar follows different systems regionally, such as the **Vikram Samvat** and **Saka Samvat**.
 
• Despite regional differences, Chaitra and Vaisakha are common months across most systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is the legislative organ of the Union Government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Parliament** is the legislative organ of the Union Government in India.
 
• It consists of two houses: the **Lok Sabha (House of the People)** and the **Rajya Sabha (Council of States)**, along with the President of India.
 
• The primary function of the Parliament is to **frame laws for the country** and amend existing laws as required.
 
• It also oversees the **executive branch**, ensuring accountability through debates, discussions, and the questioning of ministers.
 
• Key legislative powers include passing budgets, enacting laws, and addressing issues of national importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Sabha:**

 
 
• It is the lower house of Parliament and represents the people of India directly.
 
• Members are directly elected by citizens through general elections, held every five years.
 
• The Lok Sabha is responsible for introducing and passing money bills.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha:**
 
 
• It is the upper house of Parliament and represents the states and union territories of India.
 
• Members are elected by the legislative assemblies of states and union territories, and some are nominated by the President for their expertise.
 
• The Rajya Sabha reviews and suggests amendments to bills passed by the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Powers of Parliament:**
 
 
• The Parliament holds the authority to make laws on subjects listed in the Union List, Concurrent List, and, in certain cases, the State List.
 
• In cases of national emergencies, the Parliament gains greater legislative powers over state matters.
 
 
 
• **President's Role:**
 
 
• The President of India is an integral part of the Parliament and is responsible for giving assent to bills passed by both houses before they become laws.
 
• The President can also summon, prorogue, or dissolve the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following are building blocks of proteins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amino acids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amino acids** are organic compounds that serve as the building blocks of proteins in living organisms.
 
• Proteins are formed through the polymerization of amino acids via **peptide bonds**, creating long chains known as polypeptides.
 
• There are **20 standard amino acids** commonly found in proteins, which include essential and non-essential amino acids.
 
• **Essential amino acids** cannot be synthesized by the body and must be obtained through diet, whereas non-essential amino acids can be produced internally.
 
• Amino acids play crucial roles in various biological functions, including enzyme activity, cellular structure, and metabolic processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peptide Bond**: A chemical bond formed between two amino acids when the carboxyl group of one reacts with the amino group of another, releasing a molecule of water.
 
• **Protein Structure Levels**: Proteins have four structural levels—primary (sequence of amino acids), secondary (alpha-helices and beta-sheets), tertiary (three-dimensional structure), and quaternary (arrangement of multiple polypeptides).
 
• **Role of Proteins**: Proteins function as enzymes, hormones, antibodies, transport molecules, and structural components in cells and tissues.
 
• **Metabolic Pathways**: Amino acids are precursors for important biomolecules like neurotransmitters, nucleotides, and nitrogen-containing compounds.
 
• **Protein Synthesis**: The process involves transcription (DNA to mRNA) and translation (mRNA to protein), utilizing ribosomes and tRNA for the assembly of amino acids.

questions.question: Which of the following is a NOT a feature of the Indian Parliamentary form of Government?

options.text: Non membership of the ministers in Legislature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-membership of the ministers in Legislature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Parliamentary system follows the principle of **fusion of powers**, where the executive (Prime Minister and Council of Ministers) is part of the legislature.
 
• Ministers must be members of the legislature (either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha) or must get elected/nominated within six months if not already a member.
 
• The provision of ministers being non-members of the legislature is not in line with the Parliamentary system, as it is a feature of the **Presidential system** like that of the USA.
 
• The Parliamentary system is characterized by the **collective responsibility** of the Council of Ministers to the Lok Sabha, which requires them to be accountable as members of the legislature.
 
• This ensures effective coordination between the legislature and executive, a hallmark of the Indian Parliamentary democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary vs Presidential System:**

 
 
• In the Parliamentary system, there is a fusion of powers, whereas in the Presidential system, there is a strict separation of powers.
 
• In the Presidential system, ministers are not part of the legislature, unlike in the Parliamentary system.
 
 
 
• **Collective Responsibility:**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers in India operates on the principle of collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha.
 
• This means that if the government loses confidence in the Lok Sabha, all ministers must resign.
 
 
 
• **Majority Party Rule:**
 
 
• The party or coalition with the majority in the Lok Sabha forms the government in the Indian Parliamentary system.
 
• This ensures stability and reflects the will of the electorate.
 
 
 
• **Dissolution of the Lower House:**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha can be dissolved by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister, marking the end of its term.
 
• This feature allows for fresh elections and the opportunity for the electorate to choose their representatives again.

questions.question: What is the process of a substance changing directly from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sublimation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sublimation** is the process where a substance changes directly from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state.
 
• Common examples include the sublimation of **dry ice (solid carbon dioxide)** and **naphthalene balls**.
 
• This process occurs when the pressure and temperature conditions are such that the liquid state is bypassed entirely.
 
• Sublimation is commonly observed in substances with strong intermolecular forces and low vapor pressures at room temperature.
 
• The reverse process of a gas turning directly into a solid is also called sublimation or sometimes deposition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Terminology:**

 
 
• **Fusion:** The process of a solid changing into a liquid.
 
• **Evaporation:** The process of a liquid changing into a gas below its boiling point.
 
• **Condensation:** The process of a gas turning into a liquid.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sublimation:**
 
 
• Sublimation is used in the purification of substances where impurities do not sublimate.
 
• It is used in freeze-drying techniques for preserving perishable materials.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Sublimable Substances:**
 
 
• Dry ice (solid CO₂) changes directly into carbon dioxide gas.
 
• Iodine, camphor, and ammonium chloride are other common examples of substances that sublimate.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Explanation:**
 
 
• The process occurs under specific temperature and pressure conditions where the substance's triple point is bypassed.
 
• At these conditions, the solid's vapor pressure equals the surrounding pressure, leading to direct conversion to the gaseous state.

questions.question: Which type of coal is found in Damodar valley?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bituminous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bituminous coal** is the most abundant type of coal found in India and is widely used for industrial purposes.
 
• The Damodar Valley, located in eastern India, is one of the richest coal-bearing regions and primarily contains **bituminous coal deposits**.
 
• The coal in this region is known for its high carbon content and **moderate moisture levels**, making it ideal for thermal power generation and steel production.
 
• The Damodar Valley includes major coalfields such as Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro, and Giridih, which are key contributors to India's coal reserves.
 
• Bituminous coal from the Damodar Valley is also utilized in the production of coke, which is essential for metallurgical processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coal Types and Classification:**

 
 
• Coal is classified into four main types: **Anthracite, Bituminous, Lignite, and Peat**, based on carbon content and energy output.
 
• **Anthracite** is the highest grade of coal with the highest carbon content and energy efficiency.
 
• **Lignite** is a lower-grade coal with higher moisture content and lower energy efficiency.
 
• **Peat** is the earliest stage of coal formation, with the lowest carbon content and energy output.
 
 
 
• **Coalfields in India:**
 
 
• India's major coalfields are located in states like Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Jharia coalfield in Jharkhand is known for its high-grade coking coal used in steel production.
 
• The Raniganj coalfield in West Bengal is one of the oldest coalfields in India.
 
 
 
• **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC):**
 
 
• DVC was established in 1948 to manage the resources of the Damodar Valley, including coal and water.
 
• It plays a key role in power generation, irrigation, and flood control in the region.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Coal in India:**
 
 
• Coal is a major source of energy in India, contributing to over 50% of the country's electricity generation.
 
• India is the second-largest coal producer in the world, with significant reserves in the eastern and central regions.
 
• The coal industry is vital for industrial growth, particularly in sectors like steel, cement, and thermal power.

Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

__Mahira is an more efficient__ and hardworking employee of her company.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains an incorrect usage of the article "**an**" before the word "**more efficient**."
 
• The word "**more efficient**" is comparative, and the article "**an**" does not fit here grammatically.
 
• Instead, the correct usage is "**an efficient**," as "efficient" does not require the comparative "more" in this context.
 
• Thus, the appropriate substitution is **"Mahira is an efficient and hardworking employee of her company."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Mahira is an efficient and hardworking employee of her company."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Mahira is the efficient:** This option is incorrect as the use of "**the**" implies uniqueness or specificity, which is not the intended meaning here.
 
• **Mahira is the more efficient:** This option is also incorrect because it requires a comparison context which is absent in the sentence.
 
• **Mahira is an efficient:** This is the correct substitution as it ensures grammatical correctness and clarity.
</ul
